title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 27-29). Grothendieck introduces a new, finer notion of 'algebraic equivalence to 0' on a smooth variety X. A cycle is 'alg-equivalent to 0' if it is a sum of cycles of the form Z(n). Here T is a smooth, connected, projective variety, Z is a cycle on X×T (a correspondence), and n is a 0-cycle on T with deg n = 0 and S_T(n) = 0. S_T is the Albanese summation map to Alb_T. So the relation is generated by images under correspondences of Albanese kernels T(T) = ker(CH_0(T)_deg0 → Alb_T(k)). The left margin notes that projectivity of T in 1.1 is used fully here, since S_T needs T projective or else a generalized Albanese. The quotient A'^*(X) satisfies the usual functorialities (Scholie 1.3 on p.27). The relation sits between rational and classical algebraic equivalence.

Theorem 1.4 (X smooth, projective, connected, dim n). An abandoned, crossed-out opening was meant to treat dimension 0 and codimension 1 together.
(i) A 0-cycle N is equivalent to 0 iff deg N = 0 and S_X(N) = 0.
- Proof of the 'if' direction: take T = X and Z = the diagonal, so N = Z(N).
- Proof of 'only if' (cited as [ ,1.2]): a correspondence Z: T → X induces a homomorphism Alb_T → Alb_X compatible with S. Hence Z maps the Albanese kernel of T into that of X.
So on 0-cycles, A'_0(X) = Z ⊕ Alb_X(k).
(ii) A divisor D is equivalent to 0 iff it is linearly equivalent to 0.
- Linear ⇒ alg is already known.
- Conversely (p.29): Z(n) = u(S_T(n)), where u: Alb_T → Pic^0_X is the homomorphism defined by the divisor Z on X×T, via the universal property of the Albanese. So S_T(n) = 0 forces Z(n) ~_lin 0.
Thus A'^1 = Pic: the new relation recovers exactly the 'abelian-variety part' in codimension 1 and dimension 0.

Remark 1.5 asks whether, already for 0-cycles, this equivalence coincides with linear (rational) equivalence, and whether it does for all cycles ('???'). For 0-cycles this is the question whether the Albanese kernel T(X) vanishes.

Next page (Thm 1.6): the product of two classes that are algebraically trivial in the classical sense vanishes in A'^*. The key input: for smooth projective T, T', the cycle ((x)-(y))×((x')-(y')) on T×T' has Albanese sum 0, since Alb(T×T') = Alb T × Alb T'. A margin NB states that one does not know whether this cycle is rationally equivalent to 0, even when T, T' are curves. A further query asks whether 'alg-trivial · num-trivial' already suffices. In modern terms: Grothendieck defines, via correspondences, the subgroup generated by images of Albanese kernels — essentially a second step F^2 of a Bloch–Beilinson/S. Saito-type filtration built on algebraic rather than homological equivalence. He then proves F^1_alg · F^1_alg ⊂ F^2.
errors: No mathematical error in the proofs given. Over a non-algebraically-closed k, the use of points and of S_T(n) ∈ Alb_T(k) needs care, but it is fine over k = k̄.

Remark 1.5's question has a negative answer in general. Mumford (1969) showed that for a complex surface with p_g > 0 the Albanese kernel is huge (infinite-dimensional), so this equivalence differs from rational equivalence already for 0-cycles.

The margin NB on p.29 likewise has a negative answer over C. For curves T, T' of positive genus, the cycles ((x)-(y))×((x')-(y')) generate the Albanese kernel of T×T', which has p_g = g·g' > 0, so they are not all rationally trivial. Over number fields, Bloch–Beilinson predicts the opposite.
The 'proof' of (ii) is completed only on p.29. On this page the cited reference '[ ,1.2]' is left blank.

ideas.what: Adequate equivalence relation generated by images under correspondences (from smooth projective T) of Albanese kernels of 0-cycles; quotient A'^*(X)
ideas.modern_name: Correspondence-defined F^2 step of a Bloch–Beilinson / S. Saito-type filtration (relative to algebraic equivalence); 'Albanese-kernel equivalence'
ideas.usually_credited_to: S. Saito (1990s), Jannsen, Murre; Bloch for the role of Albanese kernels (1970s)

ideas.what: On 0-cycles this equivalence equals 'degree 0 and Albanese sum 0'; on divisors it equals linear equivalence
ideas.modern_name: CH_0 modulo Albanese kernel = Z ⊕ Alb; Pic via universal property of Albanese / Pic^0 duality

ideas.what: Question whether the Albanese kernel vanishes, i.e. whether the equivalence equals rational equivalence for 0-cycles and in general
Product of two algebraically trivial classes lies in the Albanese-kernel subgroup, via ((x)-(y))×((x')-(y')) having Albanese sum zero; question whether alg·num suffices
ideas.modern_name: F^1·F^1 ⊂ F^2 for the Bloch–Beilinson filtration; Bloch's product-of-curves cycles

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines, by correspondences from Albanese kernels of smooth projective T, an adequate equivalence between rational and algebraic equivalence. He computes it in codimension 1 and dimension 0, and shows that products of algebraically trivial cycles fall into it. This is an early instance of the 'second step' of the conjectural Bloch–Beilinson filtration defined via correspondences, anticipating constructions of S. Saito, Jannsen and Murre and Bloch's product-of-curves cycles.
missed.quote: Soit 𝔑 un 0-cycle sur X. Alors 𝔑 est alg-équiv. à 0 ssi 𝔑 est de degré 0, et S_X(𝔑)=0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority for the idea of filtering Chow groups by images of Albanese kernels under correspondences. Grothendieck also explicitly asks whether this relation is rational equivalence, which is the Mumford/Bloch circle of questions, probably before Mumford 1969.

missed.claim: He asks whether it suffices that one factor be algebraically trivial and the other only numerically trivial for the product to vanish in A'^*.
missed.quote: il suffit que l'un des 𝔷 soit alg. équiv. à 0, et l'autre num. équiv. à 0 ??
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This relates to the open question F^1_alg · (num-trivial) ⊂ F^2. It is tied to standard conjecture D and Bloch–Beilinson multiplicativity, and to Voevodsky-type nilpotence questions.

deep.surprise_reason: Several things are notable for c.1965–71: the correspondence-defined 'Albanese-kernel' equivalence, the statement alg·alg ⊂ it, and the explicit open questions (Albanese kernel = 0? the product-of-curves cycle rationally trivial?). These anticipate Mumford, Bloch and Saito-style filtrations. The individual results, however, are now standard and the questions were settled or reformulated by others.
transcription_corrections: 'l'équiv. d'Alb.' in Remarque 1.5 is uncertain. The ink may read 'l'équiv. alg.' (his newly defined relation), which fits the sense 'whether alg. equivalence (new sense) coincides with linear equivalence' better.
'prouvons la [?] en sens inverse' probably reads 'prouvons-le en sens inverse'.
Margin: 'ici il semble qu'on utilise à fond que dans 1.1. on prend T projectif' is consistent with the image.
